mcqs.q: Endodontics is derived from words meaning:
mcqs.explain: Endo = inside, odont = tooth; the study of the pulp and periradicular tissues.

mcqs.q: The most common cause of pulpal/periradicular disease is:
mcqs.explain: Pulp/periradicular pathosis is primarily a microbial disease, most often initiated by caries.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct order of the phases of endodontic treatment?
mcqs.explain: Access opening → cleaning & shaping → obturation → (coronal-seal) restoration.

mcqs.q: Before starting root canal treatment, the clinician should ensure that:
opts: A restorative (final restoration) plan has been approved
The tooth is definitely going to be extracted
mcqs.explain: The final restoration provides the coronal seal and is a continuum of RCT — its plan must be approved beforehand.

mcqs.q: Which is a CONTRAINDICATION to endodontic treatment?
opts: A vertical root fracture / non-restorable tooth
An apical abscess on a restorable tooth
mcqs.explain: Non-restorable teeth (VRF, deep crack, poor crown:root, severe resorption), uncooperative patients and non-strategic teeth are contraindications.

mcqs.q: Rubber dam application in the steps of RCT is done:
mcqs.explain: Order: assessment → diagnosis/plan → rubber dam → access → working length → clean & shape → obturate → coronal seal.

mcqs.q: Placing a material directly on a mechanical/traumatic vital pulp exposure is a:
mcqs.explain: Direct pulp cap = material (Ca(OH)₂/MTA) directly on an exposed vital pulp; indirect cap is over remaining caries without exposure.

mcqs.q: Removal of only the coronal portion of a vital pulp, preserving the radicular pulp, is a:
mcqs.explain: Pulpotomy removes the coronal pulp and keeps the radicular pulp vital (e.g. Cvek pulpotomy after trauma).

mcqs.q: Apexogenesis differs from apexification in that apexogenesis:
opts: Encourages continued root-end development in a VITAL tooth
Induces a calcified barrier in a NON-vital open apex
mcqs.explain: Apexogenesis = continued root development in a vital tooth; apexification = a calcified barrier in a non-vital tooth with an open apex.

mcqs.q: Agents commonly used for internal bleaching of an endodontically treated tooth are:
opts: Sodium perborate and hydrogen peroxide (or saline)
mcqs.explain: Internal bleaching uses oxidizing agents — sodium perborate with hydrogen peroxide or saline.

mcqs.q: In Fish's zones of inflammation, the zone containing polymorphs and microbes is the zone of:
mcqs.explain: Zone of infection = polymorphs + microbes; contamination has no bacteria; irritation has macrophages/osteoclasts; stimulation has fibroblasts/osteoblasts.

mcqs.q: The main objective of endodontic therapy is:
opts: Shaping and cleaning all pulp spaces, then complete obturation
Complete elimination of all bacteria from the oral cavity
Removal of the tooth once the pulp has become necrotic
Sealing the access cavity with a permanent restoration
mcqs.explain: Shaping and cleaning come first; obturation of the cleaned space with an inert material completes it.

mcqs.q: The most frequent causes of endodontic failure are:
opts: Apical percolation, incomplete canal obturation, and untreated (missed) canals
Use of rubber dam and magnification
Delayed placement of the final restoration alone
mcqs.explain: Missed canals are often the result of a lack of knowledge of the canal anatomy.

mcqs.q: Missed canals most often arise from:
opts: Lack of knowledge of the canal anatomy
Using too small a file size
mcqs.explain: This is why canal morphology is studied tooth by tooth before instrumentation.

mcqs.q: Pulp and periradicular pathosis is primarily:
mcqs.explain: Because it is microbial, removing the noxious stimulus by cleaning and filling allows inflammation to subside and healing to occur.

mcqs.q: The access opening differs from tooth to tooth according to the:
mcqs.explain: Each tooth therefore has its own access outline, determined by where the chamber and orifices lie beneath the occlusal surface.

mcqs.q: The restorative plan must be approved:
opts: Before the root canal treatment is started
At the review appointment six months later
Only if the tooth later becomes symptomatic
mcqs.explain: There is no point completing an RCT on a tooth that cannot be restored afterwards.

mcqs.q: Which step of RCT provides the coronal seal?
opts: The restoration — temporary filling or final restoration
mcqs.explain: The coronal seal protects the obturated canal from re-contamination by oral fluids.

mcqs.q: Which is an INDICATION for endodontic treatment?
opts: An uncooperative patient who refuses treatment
mcqs.explain: The other three are contraindications — two structural and one behavioural.

mcqs.q: 'Prophylactic' or elective endodontic treatment means treatment:
opts: When extraction of a restoratively hopeless tooth is not possible
Performed on every tooth before crowning
Carried out only on primary teeth
Done to relieve acute pain in an emergency
mcqs.explain: It is an optional indication, used when the tooth must be retained despite a poor restorative outlook.

mcqs.q: Which of the following makes a tooth NON-RESTORABLE and therefore contraindicates endodontic treatment?
mcqs.explain: Inadequate periodontal support, deep cracks, a poor crown:root ratio, insufficient tooth structure and severe resorption are the other non-restorable features.

mcqs.q: A well-obturated canal should extend:
opts: As close as possible to the apical constriction of each canal
Exactly 2 mm beyond the radiographic apex
mcqs.explain: Gross overextension and underfilling are both listed as faults to avoid.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT one of the faults the general objectives warn against?
mcqs.explain: An apex locator helps achieve the objective rather than violating it.

mcqs.q: An INDIRECT pulp cap is placed:
opts: On a thin partition of remaining carious dentin that, if removed, might expose the pulp
Directly onto an exposed vital pulp
Over the orifice after removing the coronal pulp
Into the canal after complete pulp extirpation
mcqs.explain: It is used in immature permanent teeth to avoid creating an exposure.

mcqs.q: A direct pulp cap seals an exposed vital pulp with:
mcqs.explain: The aim is to form reparative dentin and maintain pulp vitality.

mcqs.q: A Cvek pulpotomy is a form of:
mcqs.explain: Pulpotomy removes the coronal vital pulp to preserve the radicular portion, either for emergency relief or therapeutically.

mcqs.q: Regenerative endodontics (revascularization) is defined as:
opts: Biologically-based procedures to replace damaged pulp-dentin structures
Surgical removal of the root apex plus a retrograde filling
Chemical removal of discoloration from a treated tooth
Extraction and reinsertion of a tooth to perform treatment
mcqs.explain: It aims to restore the tissue biologically rather than merely fill the space.

mcqs.q: Root amputation is best described as:
opts: Removal of a whole root and its soft tissue, crown left intact
Removal of the apical third of a root
Extraction and reinsertion of the whole tooth
Removal of the coronal pulp only
mcqs.explain: The crown is retained and supported by the remaining root or roots.

mcqs.q: Intentional replantation involves:
opts: Extracting a tooth to perform treatment, then reinserting it into its alveolus
Transplanting a tooth into a different socket
Replacing a tooth with an implant
Repositioning a luxated tooth after trauma
mcqs.explain: It allows root-end fillings or perforation repair that cannot be done from inside the mouth.

mcqs.q: In Fish's zones of inflammation, the zone of CONTAMINATION contains:
opts: Round-cell infiltration, cellular destruction, dead bone cells and lymphocytes — but NO bacteria
Macrophages, osteoclasts and normal bone cells
mcqs.explain: Bacteria are confined to zone 1, the zone of infection.

mcqs.q: Which Fish zone contains macrophages, osteoclasts and small round cells, with collagen digested by phagocytes?
mcqs.explain: Normal bone cells are still present in this zone.

mcqs.q: In Fish's zone of STIMULATION:
opts: Fibroblasts and osteoblasts predominate and the toxin acts as a stimulant
mcqs.explain: Collagen fibres form a defensive wall around the zone of irritation and a scaffold for new bone.

mcqs.q: Which agents are most used for internal bleaching?
opts: Sodium perborate with hydrogen peroxide, or sodium perborate with saline
mcqs.explain: Internal bleaching uses chemical oxidizing agents placed within the endodontically treated tooth.

mcqs.q: Which is listed as a contraindication to endodontic treatment?
opts: A tooth with a vertical root fracture
A tooth with an irreversibly inflamed pulp
A tooth needing intentional endodontics for a prosthesis
A tooth with apical periodontitis and a sinus tract
mcqs.explain: Vertical root fracture makes the tooth non-restorable; the others are indications.

mcqs.q: Prophylactic endodontics, sometimes called elective, is indicated when:
opts: Extraction of a restoratively hopeless tooth is not possible
The pulp is irreversibly inflamed but still vital
An apical abscess has drained through the sulcus
A traumatic injury has fractured the enamel only
mcqs.explain: It is the fifth listed indication, used when extraction cannot be carried out.

mcqs.q: Which finding belongs to the non-restorable group of contraindications?
opts: A patient who refuses the proposed treatment
An oral condition that can be improved quickly
mcqs.explain: Inadequate periodontal support, vertical fracture, deep crack, poor crown-to-root ratio, insufficient structure and severe resorption.

mcqs.q: The most frequent causes of endodontic failure are:
opts: Apical percolation, incomplete obturation and untreated canals
Rubber dam leakage and inadequate anaesthesia
Excessive irrigation and sodium hypochlorite accidents
mcqs.explain: All three stem from an incomplete grasp of the root canal anatomy.

mcqs.q: Which objective of non-surgical endodontic treatment concerns the radiograph?
opts: A well-obturated system filled close to the apical constriction
Debridement and shaping of the whole root canal system
Alleviating present and preventing future signs or symptoms
Maintaining health and promoting periradicular repair
mcqs.explain: Objective (c) is specifically about the radiographic appearance of the filling.

mcqs.q: Which should be avoided according to the stated objectives?
opts: Underfilling in the presence of patent canals
Filling that reaches the apical constriction of each canal
Debriding and shaping the entire canal system
Promoting repair of the periradicular tissues
mcqs.explain: Gross overextension, underfilling with patent canals, ledges and perforations are all to be avoided.

mcqs.q: Which step of RCT immediately precedes access cavity preparation?
mcqs.explain: The order is assessment, diagnosis and plan, rubber dam, access, working length, cleaning and shaping, obturation, coronal seal.

mcqs.q: Indirect pulp capping places a material on:
opts: A thin partition of remaining carious dentin
The amputated surface of a coronal pulp
An open apex with a necrotic pulp
mcqs.explain: Removing that last layer of carious dentin might expose the pulp in an immature permanent tooth.

mcqs.q: Which procedure removes the coronal portion of a vital pulp?
mcqs.explain: Pulpotomy, or pulp amputation, preserves the vitality of the remaining radicular pulp.

mcqs.q: Apexification differs from apexogenesis in that apexification is performed on teeth with:
opts: Fully formed roots and vital pulps
mcqs.explain: Apexogenesis is a vital pulp therapy; apexification induces a calcified barrier where the pulp is necrotic.

mcqs.q: Which material is named for sealing a pulpal wound in a pulp cap?
mcqs.explain: Calcium hydroxide or MTA, to facilitate reparative dentin formation.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT one of the listed dental trauma categories?
mcqs.explain: The list runs enamel fracture, crown fracture without and with exposure, crown-root fracture, root fracture, luxation and avulsion.

mcqs.q: Intentional replantation is performed in order to:
opts: Carry out root-end filling or perforation repair outside the mouth
Reposition a tooth that was avulsed by trauma
Remove all of one root while leaving the crown supported
Induce a calcified barrier at an open apex
mcqs.explain: The tooth is deliberately extracted, treated, then reinserted into its alveolus.

mcqs.q: Root amputation is defined as surgical removal of:
opts: All of the root and adherent soft tissues, leaving the crown intact
The apical third of the root and the surrounding lesion
The crown, leaving the roots as overdenture abutments
A supernumerary distolingual root of a mandibular molar
mcqs.explain: The crown remains, supported by the remaining root or roots.

mcqs.q: The agents most frequently used for internal bleaching are:
opts: Sodium perborate with hydrogen peroxide, or with saline
mcqs.explain: Chemical oxidizing agents placed within the coronal portion of the treated tooth.

mcqs.q: Which belongs to the management of complications during root canal treatment?
opts: Incision and drainage of a swelling
mcqs.explain: Post removal, perforation repair, broken instruments and procedural errors such as ledges and transportation.

mcqs.q: Which cells characterise the zone of infection?
opts: Polymorphs, together with the microbes themselves
mcqs.explain: It is the only zone where bacteria are actually present.

mcqs.q: The zone of contamination is distinguished by:
opts: Round cell infiltration and dead bone cells, but no bacteria
Fibroblasts laying down a collagen scaffold
mcqs.explain: Cellular destruction and lymphocytes are present, but the bacteria are not.

mcqs.q: In which zone do osteoclasts resorb bone and phagocytes digest collagen?
mcqs.explain: Macrophages, osteoclasts and small round cells characterise it.

mcqs.q: In the zone of stimulation, the collagen fibres secreted by fibroblasts act as:
opts: A wall of defence and a scaffolding for new bone
A barrier that prevents any further bone formation
A medium in which bacteria are trapped and killed
A membrane that separates pulp from periodontium
mcqs.explain: The toxin acts as a stimulant at this distance, so bone is built rather than resorbed.

saqs.q: Define endodontics and state the main objective of endodontic therapy.
saqs.a: ENDODONTICS (endo = inside, odont = tooth) — the biology of the pulp and the etiology, diagnosis, prevention and treatment of pulp and periradicular disease. OBJECTIVE — shape and clean all pulp spaces, then obturate completely with an inert filling material.

rows: endo = inside, odont = tooth — the biology of the pulp, and the etiology, diagnosis, prevention and treatment of disease/injury of the pulp and periradicular tissues
thorough shaping and cleaning of ALL pulp spaces, then COMPLETE OBTURATION with an inert filling material

saqs.q: State the phases of endodontic treatment and why the final restoration matters.
saqs.a: Four phases: access opening, cleaning and shaping, obturation, restoration. The final restoration gives the CORONAL SEAL that prevents coronal microleakage, so it is a continuum of RCT and its plan is approved before treatment begins.

ans.text: The final restoration provides the CORONAL SEAL that prevents coronal microleakage — so it is a continuum of RCT, and its plan must be approved before treatment begins.

saqs.q: Give three indications and three contraindications for endodontic treatment.
saqs.a: Indications: irreversibly inflamed or necrotic pulp; apical periodontitis or abscess; prosthetic/intentional endodontics; after trauma. Contraindications: non-restorable tooth; uncooperative patient; unimprovable oral condition; non-strategic tooth.

head: Indications (any 3)
Contraindications (any 3)
rows: Non-restorable tooth (vertical root fracture, poor crown:root ratio, severe resorption)

saqs.q: Name and briefly describe Fish's four zones of inflammation.
saqs.a: 1) Infection — polymorphs and microbes. 2) Contamination — round-cell infiltrate, dead bone cells, lymphocytes, NO bacteria. 3) Irritation — macrophages and osteoclasts, collagen digested. 4) Stimulation — fibroblasts and osteoblasts, collagen walls off and scaffolds new bone.

head: Zone
Contents
rows: round-cell infiltrate, cellular destruction, dead bone cells, lymphocytes — but no bacteria
macrophages and osteoclasts; collagen digested by phagocytes, bone cells normal
fibroblasts and osteoblasts; the toxin acts as a stimulant and collagen forms a defensive wall and scaffold for new bone

saqs.q: Define vital pulp therapy and name the procedures it includes.
saqs.a: VITAL PULP THERAPY preserves a pulp compromised by trauma, caries or restorative procedures in a healthy state. It includes indirect pulp cap, direct pulp cap, pulpotomy, apexogenesis and apexification.

ans.text: VITAL PULP THERAPY — treatment aimed at preserving and maintaining a pulp compromised by trauma, caries or restorative procedures in a healthy state.

head: Procedure
What it is
rows: material placed on a thin partition of remaining carious dentin that, if removed, might expose the pulp
sealing an exposed vital pulp with calcium hydroxide or MTA to form reparative dentin
removal of the coronal vital pulp to preserve the radicular portion (e.g. Cvek pulpotomy after trauma)
inducing a calcified barrier in an open apex of a necrotic immature tooth

saqs.q: State the general objectives of nonsurgical endodontic treatment.
saqs.a: (a) Alleviate present and prevent future signs and symptoms. (b) Debride and shape the root-canal system. (c) Create a well-obturated canal as close as possible to the apical constriction. (d) Maintain health and promote periradicular healing.

list: (a) Alleviate present and prevent future signs and symptoms
(b) Debride and shape the root-canal system
(c) Create a well-obturated canal, as close as possible to the apical constriction of each canal
(d) Maintain health and promote healing of the periradicular tissues — avoiding gross overextension, underfilling, ledges and perforations

saqs.q: Describe the scope of surgical endodontics.
saqs.a: Root amputation, intentional replantation and repair of resorption; plus incision and drainage, biopsy, and management of complications (post removal, perforation repair, broken instruments, ledges and transportation), with implants as the alternative.

head: Procedure
What it is
rows: removal of a whole root and its soft tissue, the crown left intact on the remaining root(s)
extracting a tooth to treat it (root-end filling, perforation repair) then reinserting it
exposure, debridement and restoration of a resorptive defect on the root surface

ans.text: Also incision and drainage and biopsy; and management of complications — post removal, perforation repair, broken instruments, ledges and transportation — with implants as the alternative when the tooth cannot be saved.

saqs.q: What is regenerative endodontics, and what is internal bleaching used for?
saqs.a: REGENERATIVE ENDODONTICS (revascularization): biologically-based procedures to physiologically replace damaged dentin, root structures and the pulp-dentin complex. INTERNAL BLEACHING: chemical oxidizing agents inside a treated tooth to remove discoloration — sodium perborate with hydrogen peroxide or with saline.

rows: biologically-based procedures intended to physiologically replace damaged structures — dentin, root structures and the pulp-dentin complex
chemical oxidizing agents inside an endodontically-treated tooth to remove discoloration; usually sodium perborate + hydrogen peroxide, or sodium perborate + saline

saqs.q: List the indications and the contraindications for endodontic treatment.
saqs.a: Indications: pulp disease (irreversibly inflamed or necrotic pulp); apical disease (apical periodontitis or abscess); prosthetic indications or intentional endodontics; after some traumatic dental injuries; and prophylactic endodontics when extraction of a restoratively hopeless tooth is not possible. Contraindications: non-restorable teeth (inadequate periodontal support, vertical root fracture, deep crack, poor crown-to-root ratio, insufficient tooth structure, severe resorption); uncooperative patients or those refusing treatment; poor oral condition that cannot be improved within a reasonable period; and a non-strategic tooth.

list: Pulp disease — irreversibly inflamed or necrotic pulp
Apical disease — apical periodontitis or apical abscess
Prophylactic (elective) endodontics — when extraction of a restoratively hopeless tooth is not possible
Non-restorable teeth — inadequate periodontal support, vertical root fracture, deep crack, poor crown-to-root ratio, insufficient tooth structure, severe resorption
Uncooperative patients, or those who refuse treatment
Poor oral condition that cannot be improved within a reasonable period

saqs.q: State the general objectives of non-surgical endodontic treatment, and what should be avoided.
saqs.a: To alleviate present and prevent future adverse clinical signs or symptoms; to debride and shape the root canal system; to create the radiographic appearance of a well-obturated system with the filling extending as close as possible to the apical constriction of each canal; and to maintain health and promote healing and repair of the periradicular tissues. Gross overextension, underfilling in the presence of patent canals, ledges and perforations should be avoided.

list: a. Alleviate present and prevent future adverse clinical signs or symptoms.
b. Debride and shape the root canal system.
c. Create the radiographic appearance of a well-obturated system, the filling extending as close as possible to the apical constriction of each canal.
d. Maintain health and promote healing and repair of periradicular tissues.

ans.text: Avoid: gross overextension, underfilling in the presence of patent canals, ledges and perforations.

saqs.q: List the eight steps of root canal treatment in order.
saqs.a: Clinical and radiographic assessment; diagnosis and treatment plan; rubber dam application; access cavity preparation; working length determination; cleaning and shaping by instrumentation and irrigation; obturation; and coronal seal.

saqs.q: Define the procedures that make up vital pulp therapy.
saqs.a: Indirect pulp capping places a material on a thin partition of remaining carious dentin that, if removed, might expose the pulp in immature permanent teeth. Direct pulp capping places a dental material directly on a mechanical or traumatic vital pulp exposure. A pulp cap seals the pulpal wound with calcium hydroxide or MTA to facilitate reparative dentin and maintain a vital pulp. Pulpotomy is removal of the coronal portion of a vital pulp to preserve the radicular portion. Apexogenesis encourages continued physiological development and formation of the root end. Apexification induces a calcified barrier in a root with an open apex in teeth with necrotic pulps.

Definition

material placed directly on a mechanical or traumatic vital pulp exposure
sealing the pulpal wound with calcium hydroxide or MTA to facilitate reparative dentin
removal of the coronal portion of a vital pulp, preserving the radicular portion
encourages continued physiological development and formation of the root end — a vital procedure

saqs.q: Describe the four zones of inflammation and what is found in each.
saqs.a: Zone of infection: polymorphs and microbes. Zone of contamination: round cell infiltration, cellular destruction, no bacteria, dead bone cells and lymphocytes. Zone of irritation: macrophages, osteoclasts and small round cells, with collagen digested by phagocytic cells. Zone of stimulation: fibroblasts and osteoblasts with normal bone cells, the toxin acting as a stimulant, and collagen fibres forming a wall of defence around the zone of irritation and a scaffolding on which new bone is built.

head: Zone
Contents
rows: round cell infiltration · cellular destruction · no bacteria · dead bone cells · lymphocytes
macrophages · osteoclasts · small round cells — collagen digested by phagocytic cells
fibroblasts and osteoblasts · normal bone cells — collagen acts as a wall of defence and a scaffolding for new bone

ans.text: Reading outward: bacteria present, then destruction without bacteria, then resorption, then new bone being laid down.
